system_map.overview: The CAS Runner is a Python CLI application for managing architectural knowledge and governance. It follows a layered architecture: a CLI entry point (presentation), a flow runner and service layer (application), domain models in governance and steering modules (domain), and infrastructure clients for LLM and workspace initialization (infrastructure). The knowledge base is stored in a structured directory (cas-knowledge) with global, project, runtime, and template components.

layers.name: application
layers.purpose: Orchestration of workflows and use cases

layers.name: domain
layers.purpose: Core business entities and governance logic

layers.name: infrastructure
layers.purpose: External client adapters and workspace bootstrapping

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: Uses Pydantic models to define domain entities with validation and serialization.
patterns.intent: Represent business concepts as typed, validated data structures.
patterns.context: The project depends on Pydantic 2.12.5 and defines models in governance and steering modules.
patterns.solution: Define Pydantic BaseModel subclasses for each domain entity (e.g., GovernanceAction, CapabilityRecord). Use field types and validators to enforce constraints.
implementation_signals: Symbols in governance/models.py: GovernanceAction, ComplianceFinding, GovernanceHealth

costs: Schema migration overhead when domain evolves
Can lead to over-complex models if not disciplined
failure_modes: Models becoming tightly coupled to persistence details
Validation logic scattered in multiple places

patterns.reuse_notes: Reusable for any domain-heavy Python application that requires robust data validation.

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: A registry that centralizes state transition rules for governance actions.
patterns.intent: Manage allowed state transitions without scattered if-else logic.
patterns.context: Governance actions likely move through states (e.g., proposed, approved, retired). The TransitionRegistry provides a lookup map.
forces: Need to enforce valid state changes
Avoid hardcoding transition logic in many places
patterns.solution: Implement a registry mapping transition keys (e.g., (current_state, event)) to target states or handler functions.

benefits: Easy to extend with new transitions
costs: Potential for missing transitions if registry incomplete
failure_modes: Registry can become a bottleneck if not maintained
Implicit state machine may be hard to visualize

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any domain with explicit state machines (e.g., workflow engines).

patterns.name: Service Layer Orchestration
patterns.summary: A dedicated service class coordinates governance operations.
patterns.intent: Decouple use case workflows from the CLI and infrastructure details.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionService likely orchestrates actions using the engine, compliance checks, and persistence.
forces: Reusable business operations across entry points
patterns.solution: Create a service class that exposes high-level methods (e.g., execute_action, evaluate_compliance) and coordinates domain objects.

costs: May become a god class if not split by domain
failure_modes: Service bloat with too many responsibilities
Tight coupling if service directly accesses infrastructure

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard DDD service pattern; use for non-trivial use cases.

patterns.name: External Client Adapter
patterns.summary: Provides interchangeable adapters for external LLM services.
patterns.intent: Allow the rest of the system to use LLM functionality without coupling to a specific provider.
patterns.context: Both LiteLLMClient and MockLLClient exist, likely implementing a common interface.
forces: Need for testability without real LLM calls
Ability to switch providers or use local mocks
patterns.solution: Define a protocol or base class for LLM clients and implement concrete adapters (real and mock).
implementation_signals: Symbols: LiteLLMClient, MockLLClient in llm/ module

costs: May need to handle provider-specific features
failure_modes: Interface becomes too generic or too narrow
Mock behavior diverges from real behavior

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any external service (APIs, databases) where multiple implementations are needed.

patterns.name: Bootstrap Workspace Initialization
patterns.summary: A bootstrap routine initializes workspace structure and applies governance configuration.
patterns.intent: Ensure a consistent project layout and merge governance blocks into existing config.
patterns.context: bootstrap.py provides functions to set up the environment, likely creating directories and merging YAML blocks.
forces: Centralized governance configuration in a reusable block
patterns.solution: Provide a `bootstrap` function that calls `init_workspace` (creates dirs) and `merge_cas_governance_block` (merges governance YAML).

costs: May be rigid if not configurable
Merge logic can overwrite user changes if naive
failure_modes: Non-idempotent initialization may corrupt existing workspaces

patterns.reuse_notes: Use for tools that need to set up a project skeleton.

patterns.name: Knowledge Artifact Repository Structure
patterns.summary: A standardized directory hierarchy for storing knowledge artifacts (global, projects, runtime, templates).
patterns.intent: Organize architecture knowledge in a predictable way to support reuse and retrieval.
patterns.context: cas-knowledge directory contains subdirectories for global (decisions, patterns, rules), projects, runtime (traces, evaluations), and templates.
patterns.solution: Define a directory structure with well-known subdirectories and provide templates for new artifacts.

costs: Can become deeply nested, making navigation harder
failure_modes: Inconsistent subfolder usage if not enforced
Redundant artifacts if not properly indexed

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to knowledge management systems with document-centric storage.

patterns.name: Health Calculation Model
patterns.summary: Simple pattern for calculating health status from metrics and providing reasons.
patterns.intent: Provide a lightweight way to assess system health based on configurable thresholds.
patterns.context: health_model.py defines HealthStatus enum and functions to calculate health.
patterns.solution: Define an enum for health states, a function that evaluates metrics and returns status, and a function for human-readable reasons.

benefits: Easy to extend with new metrics
costs: May be overly simplified for complex systems
failure_modes: Health status can be misleading if inputs incomplete

patterns.reuse_notes: Common pattern for dashboards and monitoring.

patterns.name: Compliance Engine
patterns.summary: Dedicated engine for evaluating artifacts against governance rules.
patterns.intent: Centralize compliance checking so that rules are easily added and evaluated.
patterns.context: ComplianceEngine likely accepts rules and data, returning findings.
forces: Keep validation separate from business logic
patterns.solution: Implement a class that takes a set of rules and an artifact, applies the rules, and returns compliance findings.

costs: Potential performance issues with many rules
failure_modes: Rules can become outdated or conflicting
Engine may become a monolith if not split

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful for any system with business rules or regulations.

patterns.name: Steering Data Models
patterns.summary: Rich data models for capturing capability, lineage, and architectural deltas.
patterns.intent: Model complex steering information in a structured and extensible way.
patterns.context: steering/models.py contains many dataclasses and Pydantic models representing capabilities, git deltas, and more.
patterns.solution: Define models with appropriate relationships (e.g., using Pydantic for validation) to store and retrieve steering data.
implementation_signals: Symbols: RawGitDelta, CapabilityRecord, CapabilitySet, CapabilityLineage, ArchitecturalDelta
patterns.reuse_notes: Useful for domains requiring detailed tracking (e.g., capability management).

anti_patterns.name: OS metadata files committed
suggested_remediation: Add .DS_Store to .gitignore and remove from tracking

anti_patterns.name: Documentation fragmentation
symptoms: Multiple top-level documentation files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, README.md, DESIGN.md, ARCHITECTURE.md) with likely overlapping content
impact: Confusion about which doc is authoritative
suggested_remediation: Consolidate into a single structured docs folder
Use cross-references and a single source of truth

anti_patterns.name: Deeply nested knowledge structure
impact: Can make navigation and discovery difficult
Risk of inconsistency if not enforced
suggested_remediation: Enforce via Lint or CI checks

anti_patterns.name: Duplicate configuration files
symptoms: Similar config files across agent directories (.agents/, .claude/, cas-brain/.github/)

anti_patterns.name: Potential service layer bloat
symptoms: Multiple governance-related classes (Engine, Service, Merger) could overlap in responsibilities
